description: The prompt says: where a conditions-adjusted or conditions-neutral figure exists, treat it as the fairer read and prefer it over the raw one. This is the difference between telling a runner they got slower over a hot summer and telling them they held on. Guards the clause that stops a good block reading as a bad one.

vars.question: Was that pace real, or was it the heat?
vars.factLines:
Actual pace · 90 days: 6:03/mi
Cool-weather equivalent: 5:54/mi (−9s)
What the conditions were worth: 9 s/mi
Average dew point: 71°F (adjustment applied)
Coverage: 24 sessions over 90 days (high confidence) — the heat adjustment is a model, not a measurement
